findings.reason: the record the node must write is anchored to a population count the plan's own assignments contradict, so either the pooled table and the decision disagree in the same document or the worker drops a section on a guess.
findings.text: the lead decision cites a pooled population of 17 sections, but `paired-replay-assignment.json` excludes only s4 (nine replayed sections) and assignment 2 excludes only lane s53, leaving nine further sections (s10, s1, s58, s9, s139, s135, s5, s7, s100), each with clive, clive-anchored, omp-local and clive-replicate in its `replays` map — eighteen local sections, and the run store holds replay runs for all eighteen. The done-when asks the node to pool "over every replayed section", so the worker will produce an eighteen-section table beside a decision that states seventeen, and cannot tell which section the plan drops.

findings.reason: the removal is a substantial implementation whose gate (suite delta plus grep) is independent of the record's gate (query reproduces the table); one node's verdict either hides a removal defect behind a correct record or blocks the record on a deletion failure.
findings.text: s8's done-when now bundles the measurement deliverable (a pooled per-arm record carrying the lead's decision) with a repo-wide removal of the anchored edit tool across `reckon/anchored_edit.py`, the flight schema and its generated copies, `_backends.py`, `_worker_fence.py`, `dispatch_launch.py`, `prompts.py`, `capabilities.py`, `dispatch.py`, `dispatch_sessions.py`, `dispatching/`, `pyproject.toml`, three deleted test files and the other tests that name the key. Two such different verdicts — a query's output and a deletion's clean grep plus suite delta — cannot be closed on one verdict and a failure in either cannot be attributed.

findings.reason: the removal's control does falsify the key's absence, which is the change the section makes; the missing control tightens the record's evidence but does not redirect the work.

findings.reason: the explicit supersession sentence already gives the done-when precedence, so the reader is told which rule governs; removing the retained text is tidying rather than a change of what the node does.
findings.text: the retained "Superseded rule, kept for the record" paragraph states that a treatment whose interval overlaps the same-arm spread "is not adopted: it stays in the code with its setting unchanged", which directly contradicts the done-when's removal of the anchored tool, whose own figures (+6.6% input, every interval overlapping) put the tool squarely in that not-separated case. The one sentence "The rest of this section's text is superseded by the done-when below where they differ" resolves it, but a worker scanning the section in order meets the contradiction as live instruction.
